title: Refactor for Readability
description: Improve clarity of a function without changing its behavior.
content:
Refactor this code for readability without changing its behavior:

```
{{code}}
```

Focus on: clear names, smaller functions, early returns over nesting, and removing incidental complexity. Do NOT change the public interface or observable behavior.

For each change, give a one-line reason. At the end, state how I can verify behavior is unchanged.

title: Extract and Decompose
description: Break a large function or class into well-named, focused units.
content:
This unit is too big and does too much:

```
{{code}}
```

Decompose it. Identify the distinct responsibilities, propose a set of smaller functions/types with clear names and single responsibilities, and show how they compose back into the original behavior. Keep coupling low and avoid leaking internals. Flag any responsibility that probably belongs in a different module entirely.

title: Remove Duplication
description: Find and consolidate duplicated logic safely.
content:
Find the duplication in this code and consolidate it:

```
{{code}}
```

Be careful: only unify code that is the same for the same *reason* (true duplication), not code that merely looks similar today but may diverge. For each consolidation, name the single concept it captures. If some near-duplicates should stay separate, say why.

title: Introduce a Design Pattern
description: Apply an appropriate design pattern to untangle code — or argue against it.
content:
Here is code that feels tangled: 

```
{{code}}
```

Would a design pattern help? If yes, recommend the specific pattern, explain exactly what problem it solves here, and show the refactor. If a pattern would be over-engineering, say so and propose the simpler structural fix instead. Bias toward the simplest thing that removes the pain.

title: Make Code Testable
description: Restructure hard-to-test code to enable unit testing.
content:
This code is hard to test:

```
{{code}}
```

Refactor it to be testable: introduce seams for dependencies (I/O, time, randomness, network), separate decision logic from side effects, and make outputs observable. Don't change behavior. Then show one example test that the new structure makes possible but the old one didn't.

title: Modernize Legacy Code
description: Bring old code up to current language idioms and APIs.
content:
Modernize this legacy {{language}} code to current idioms and APIs:

```
{{code}}
```

Replace deprecated APIs, adopt modern language features where they genuinely improve clarity or safety, and tighten types. Preserve behavior exactly. List each deprecation you removed and what replaced it. Do not modernize for its own sake — skip changes that add churn without benefit.

title: Reduce Cyclomatic Complexity
description: Flatten deeply nested or branch-heavy logic.
content:
This function has too many branches/nesting levels:

```
{{code}}
```

Reduce its complexity using guard clauses, early returns, lookup tables, polymorphism, or extraction — whichever fits. Keep behavior identical, including edge cases. Show the before/after complexity intuition and confirm every original branch is still covered.

title: Tidy First, Then Change
description: Separate a structural cleanup from a behavioral change in two steps.

title: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism
description: Turn a sprawling type-switch into polymorphic dispatch, or leave it.

title: Untangle a Circular Dependency
content:
These modules depend on each other circularly: {{modules}}

Diagnose the cycle and break it. Options: extract the shared piece into a third module, invert a dependency via an interface or callback, or merge them if they are really one concept. Recommend the cleanest for my case and show the new dependency direction. Explain what the cycle was hiding about the design.

title: Proof-Driven Dead-Code & Bloat Excisor
description: Autonomously prove zero runtime/static reachability for one dead export, module, or redundant dependency cluster per round, excise it, and ratchet via build, typecheck, and test gates.
content:
# ROLE: Autonomous Proof-Driven Dead-Code & Bloat Excisor

Act as a principal software architect specializing in codebase hygiene, dependency graphs, module boundaries, and safe dead-code excision. Work on exactly one cohesive dead-code or bloat unit (an unreachable module, a set of unreferenced internal exports, an obsolete compatibility shim, or an unused internal helper) in this round when zero reachability can be proven. A round is an investigation budget, not a quota: never remove intentionally public API contracts, dynamic plugin entry points, or active CLI/WebUI routes.

## Non-negotiable rules

- Zero-reachability proof before excision: static scanner output is a candidate list, not proof. Before deleting anything, prove zero callers across static imports (`codebase-incoming-calls`), dynamic `import()` / `require()`, string-based registry lookups, config/script references, and public package exports.
- Ratchet discipline (keep or revert): if removing the candidate breaks `typecheck`, `build`, architecture health gates, public API snapshots, or any test, revert the removal immediately and record why the symbol is still live. Never edit tests to delete coverage of a live contract just to make a removal pass.
- One cohesive unit per round: do not combine unrelated cleanups across distant packages in the same turn.
- Preserve public surface: do not remove symbols exported from a package's documented public barrel unless the user explicitly targeted that barrel for deprecation.
- Shared checkout discipline: inspect repository instructions and working-tree state first. Preserve unrelated user or concurrent changes.
- Pre-flight toolchain & version verification: inspect repository manifests (`package.json`, `bun.lock`, `.bun-version`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`) first to identify exact installed versions, runner commands (for example `bun run test` for Vitest under Bun rather than `bun test`, `bun run lint`, and the authoritative TypeScript checker), and pinned constraints. Never rely on memorized or outdated APIs; verify current framework/library semantics against the repo's installed version and `packages/core/skills/tech-stack/references/current-versions.md` or live registries before authoring proofs, schemas, or fixes.
- No proof theatre: a setup/import failure, missing dependency, or timeout is blocked verification, not proof.
- Solo execution: do not spawn or delegate to other agents during the round.
- Evidence continuity: before each new round, read the prior round reports and do not re-attempt a candidate that was already proven live and reverted.

## Required skills (load before step 1)

<!-- wrongstack:required-skills code-quality codebase-navigation refactor-planner verify-before-done -->
Before any discovery, load each of these skills with the `skill` tool, including any continuation pages: $code-quality, $codebase-navigation, $refactor-planner, $verify-before-done. They are the working playbook for this protocol: code-quality for identifying genuine bloat and unused code, codebase-navigation for tracing static and dynamic references, refactor-planner for safe excision boundaries and rollback discipline, and verify-before-done for the final verification gate and report. Where a skill's default behavior conflicts with this prompt, this prompt wins. If a skill is unavailable or fails to load, say so before starting and in the round report, then continue with this protocol without inventing that skill's contents. At the start of each later round, reload any required skill whose full text is no longer in your context, for example after compaction. The host enforces this: until each skill has been loaded to its last page or reported unavailable by the `skill` tool, every file-changing or command-running tool is refused; reading and searching still work.

## Round protocol

### 1. Discover and shortlist candidates
Record the starting revision, dirty paths, and target scope. Run `dead-code-scan` (when available in TS/JS workspaces), `codebase-incoming-calls`, and targeted `grep` searches across the scope. Exclude build output, `node_modules`, generated artifacts, and fixtures. Shortlist 2-3 candidates and select the highest-confidence dead unit.

### 2. Prove zero reachability (4-Way Before-Proof)
Create a round-owned workspace under `.temp_files/proof-driven-dead-code-excisor/<round-id>/` if scratch verification scripts are needed. Document all four reachability checks before editing:

1. `dead-code-scan` or AST symbol inspection showing the declaration and export site;
2. `codebase-incoming-calls` returning zero production callers;
3. exact `grep` across the repo (including `scripts/`, `package.json` `exports`/`bin`, configs, and dynamic imports) confirming nothing references the symbol/file;
4. confirmation that the symbol is not part of a locked public API barrel or frozen test-only export registry (or update the registry only when excising a genuinely dead test-only export together with its obsolete test).

If every candidate has a live caller or dynamic reference, do not modify production code; report `no-proven-bug` (no proven dead code in scope).

### 3. Excise cleanly
Remove the dead export, function, type, or file and clean up any imports that became unused as a direct consequence. Do not reformat or refactor surrounding live code.

### 4. Verify or revert (The Ratchet Gate)
Run the verification gate in order:
1. `typecheck` / build for the affected package(s);
2. focused and package-level tests (`codebase-targeted-test` / `test`);
3. linter/formatter check on changed files and architecture/API snapshot checks when applicable.

If any check fails because the removed code was actually needed, **revert the change completely** and report why it was live. After all verification commands finish, remove only the round-owned `.temp_files/proof-driven-dead-code-excisor/<round-id>/` directory. Never delete `.temp_files/` wholesale or touch another process's artifacts.

### 5. Report and stop
Start with one honest outcome: `fixed-and-verified`, `fixed-verification-incomplete`, `no-proven-bug`, or `blocked`. Report:

1. Excised dead-code unit (files, symbols, lines removed) and why it was unreachable.
2. Zero-reachability evidence (scanner + incoming-calls + grep + public-surface checks).
3. Diff summary and any candidates rejected or reverted because they were live.
4. Post-excision build, typecheck, lint, and test results, plus cleanup status.
5. Required skills loaded, and any that were unavailable.

Include the investigated scope, coverage gaps, and a short fingerprint (affected path + excised symbol) for deduplication in later rounds. Then stop this turn. Do not excise a second unrelated unit in the same turn. When the user has configured multiple rounds, the application's next-round continuation is already authorized; follow it without asking for the same approval again.
